headline: No direct interaction pathway is documented; the main residual risk is low prompt-injection/data-flow exposure if outputs are manually bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile shows a shared channel, and B cannot read files or use MCP, so direct injection is blocked. However, A is a content-writing prompt repository and B is a game-playing agent; if an operator manually copies A-generated prompts into B, malicious instructions could ride along. This is a manual bridge risk, not a default one.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-produced prompt text into B's input, THEN injection content can influence B.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is introduced, THEN the pathway becomes stronger.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Do not paste A outputs into B without review.
Add a short human review step before any prompt transfer.
Disable shared clipboard syncing between the two environments.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has network egress none; B also has no filesystem read/write, no browser, no shell, and no network egress. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal shown, there is no plausible data exfiltration path between them in the documented configuration.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is later mounted, THEN leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent is given network egress, THEN outbound leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Review any future permission changes before enabling them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, shell, or git capabilities in the profile, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Since neither agent can mutate the same resource, there is no write-write conflict pathway to manage.
conditions: IF A gains filesystem or git write capability, THEN conflict analysis must be repeated.
IF B is reconfigured with write access, THEN overlapping writes could emerge.
mitigations: Do not grant A any filesystem or git access.
Re-check the pair after any permission change.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a prompt repository, so its outputs can be treated as reusable instructions; B is a game-playing agent and not documented as acting on external facts. The main cascade is manual: if an operator feeds A's prompts into B without checking, B may follow poor instructions. Because no autonomous downstream action is shown, the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF A's text is used as authoritative instructions for B, THEN errors can cascade.
IF B is connected to an action-taking wrapper, THEN the impact increases.
mitigations: Require human review of any A-to-B transfer.
Label A outputs as untrusted templates.
Keep B disconnected from action-taking wrappers.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either profile, and both profiles show no touched data classes. With only docs-level metadata and no regulated data flow, there is no compliance breach pathway to substantiate.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later introduced, THEN compliance review is required.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdictional constraint, THEN residency checks must be added.
mitigations: Document any regulated data before deployment.
Reassess if residency or retention requirements change.
